title: Restriction of cocartesian lifts along a base functor
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functors and degreewise pullbacks of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and inner fibrations, cocartesian fibrations and horn-cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $p:E\to B$ be an inner fibration of quasicategories in a fixed universe and let $h:T\to B$ be a functor from a quasicategory. Suppose that for every vertex $t\in T$, every $x\in E$ with $p(x)=h(t)$, and every edge $\alpha:t\to t'$ of $T$, there is a $p$-cocartesian edge with source $x$ and image exactly $h(\alpha)$. Form $P=T\times_B E$, with projections $r:P\to T$ and $j:P\to E$. Then $P$ is a quasicategory, $r$ is a cocartesian fibration, and an edge $v$ of $P$ is $r$-cocartesian if and only if $j(v)$ is $p$-cocartesian. The assertion includes $T=\Delta^1$, degenerate $h$, empty fibers, and $T=\Delta^0$; it does not assume that $p$ has cocartesian lifts of base edges outside the image of $h$.

source.place: Higher Topos Theory, Proposition 2.4.1.3(2), Remark 2.4.1.12 and Remark 2.4.2.13, opposite-category duals (preservation and reflection after restriction when global lifts of the image edges exist); Definition 2.4.2.1 and Proposition 2.4.2.3(2). Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: For an inner-horn lifting problem against $r$ with prescribed simplex $\beta:\Delta^n\to T$, project its horn to $E$. Its image under $p$ is $h\beta$ on the horn, so the inner-fibration property of $p$ supplies an $E$-simplex over exactly $h\beta$. Pairing it with $\beta$ gives a filler in the degreewise pullback $P$. Thus $r$ is an inner fibration. For an inner horn in $P$ without a prescribed base simplex, first fill its $T$-component using that $T$ is a quasicategory and apply the same construction. Hence $P$ is a quasicategory. The operators on these pairs act coordinatewise by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Definition 2.4.2.1 and Proposition 2.4.2.3(2), pullback of an inner fibration and quasicategory.

proof.text: Let $v$ be any edge of $P$ whose $E$-component $j(v)$ is $p$-cocartesian. Consider a lifting problem $a:\Lambda_0^n\to P$, $\beta:\Delta^n\to T$ for $r$, with $n\geq2$, $a|_{\{0,1\}}=v$ and $ra=\beta|_{\Lambda_0^n}$. Its projection $ja$ is a horn in $E$ over $h\beta$, with distinguished edge $j(v)$. The horn-cocartesian definition in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] gives a filler $\gamma:\Delta^n\to E$ with $p\gamma=h\beta$ and $\gamma|_{\Lambda_0^n}=ja$. The pair $(\beta,\gamma)$ is a simplex of $P$ extending $a$ over $\beta$. This verifies every required outer horn, so $v$ is $r$-cocartesian.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.1.3(2), opposite-category dual, written directly with the outer-horn definition.

proof.text: For a vertex $(t,x)$ of $P$ and an edge $\alpha:t\to t\prime$ in $T$, the stated hypothesis gives a $p$-cocartesian edge $e:x\to y$ with $p(e)=h(\alpha)$ exactly. Its endpoints satisfy $p(y)=h(t\prime)$, so $(\alpha,e)$ is an edge of the degreewise pullback with source $(t,x)$. Step 2 makes it $r$-cocartesian. Together with the inner fibration in step 1, this is precisely the cocartesian-fibration definition in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations].

source.place: Definition 2.4.2.1, cocartesian dual; image-edge form of the base-change argument in Proposition 2.4.2.3(2).

proof.text: For reflection let $v:(t,x)\to(t\prime,y)$ be $r$-cocartesian, and put $\alpha=r(v)$. Choose a $p$-cocartesian $e:x\to y\prime$ over $h(\alpha)$ as in step 3. Then $\widetilde e=(\alpha,e)$ and $v$ are both $r$-cocartesian lifts of $\alpha$ with source $(t,x)$. The lift-category and initiality clauses of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality], applied to the inner fibration $r$ between the quasicategories of step 1, make both lifts initial in $L((t,x),\alpha)$. Its universal comparison from $\widetilde e$ to $v$ gives a triangle in $P$ with first edge $\widetilde e$, second edge $c:(t\prime,y\prime)\to(t\prime,y)$, and long edge $v$, lying over the degenerate triangle with edges $\alpha,1_{t\prime},\alpha$ in $T$. The same cited statement says that $c$ is an equivalence in the fiber $P_{t\prime}$. Thus its inverse and the two inverse triangles map under $j$ to inverse data for $j(c)$ in $E$, by the simplicial-map and equivalence definitions in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Remark 2.4.1.9 and Remark 2.4.2.13, opposite-category duals; compare the chosen global lift with the restricted lift.

proof.text: Apply the initial-outer-horn clause of [lem-cbc-inner-fibration-equivalence-outer-horn-lift] to $p:E\to B$ and the equivalence $j(c)$. For every $\Lambda_0^n$ lifting problem over $B$ with edge $01=j(c)$ it supplies a filler, so $j(c)$ is $p$-cocartesian by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Project the triangle of step 4 to $E$; its first edge is $e$, second edge $j(c)$, and long edge $j(v)$. The first edge is $p$-cocartesian by its choice. The composition clause of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] now says that the second edge is $p$-cocartesian if and only if the long edge is. Hence $j(v)$ is $p$-cocartesian, completing the reverse implication.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 4.4.2.13 (Tag 01H0), initial-horn dual, followed by HTT Proposition 2.4.1.7, cocartesian dual.

proof.text: Every construction above is relative to a specified simplex of $T$ and therefore also works for constant $h$, for $T=\Delta^1$, and for $T=\Delta^0$. In the last case $P$ is the degreewise fiber of $p$. If a fiber is empty, there is no source vertex there for the lift condition, and no horn there to fill; whenever a source exists, the stated hypothesis supplies the endpoint in step 3. If $T$ is empty then $P$ is empty and all horn and lift requirements are vacuous. No choice in the proof asks for a lift of an edge of $B$ outside the image of $h$.

source.place: Definition 2.4.2.1 and the preceding degreewise horn arguments, including empty fibers and constant base maps.
